scenarios.title: Keep project access consistent across entitlement grace
plannedActions: Finish the original membership journey and retain its original rows. Rejoin member/viewer, assign viewer role and create one new owner-held team project through public HTTP.

Seed each of seven entitlement tuples in turn: active/future-paid, trialing/future-paid, past_due/future-paid, active/recently-expired, canceled/recent-cancel plus old-paid, canceled/old-cancel plus recent-paid, active/old-paid without cancel.
For each tuple, GET the project as owner, member and viewer; check exact public project shape or exact 402. GET member identity; check project inclusion/omission and team role/status/plan.
In recent active expiry, attempt a fresh member project create; in old cancellation, attempt a fresh owner project create. Require exact 402 and complete declared business-state preservation.

After the last expired-grace tuple, list the existing project as owner, then archive it through the owner route. Observe only its archive/update timestamps change; owner listing becomes empty and direct lookup is 404.

Restore only the three fixture entitlement fields, leave both rejoined memberships through their own HTTP DELETEs, and read owner team. Preserve every original declared row exactly plus the one newly archived project; finish at 80 HTTP requests and zero outbound.
expectedOutcomes: Seven explicitly seeded entitlement states are exercised through 21 real project reads and seven member identity reads. Active and trialing future-paid teams project premium access; past_due with future paid_until does not. Recent expiry and recent cancellation allow member/viewer metadata reads with canWrite false; dates safely beyond the 30-day grace window refuse those reads with exact 402 and omit the project from member identity. The owner reads the existing project in every state. canWrite assertions concern public capability projection, not document-write execution.

Cancellation time takes precedence over paid_until for grace: recent canceled_at with 31-day-old paid_until allows member/viewer reads, whereas 31-day-old canceled_at with recent paid_until refuses them. With canceled_at null, old paid_until refuses them. The real clock is not altered and exact equality at the expiry boundary is not tested. All declared business rows remain unchanged by each phase of reads and refused creates.

A member cannot create a new team project while active entitlement is expired, and the owner cannot create one after canceled grace has expired; both return exact 402 without business-row changes. Nevertheless, after grace the owner can list and archive the existing team project. Archive changes only that project archived_at and updated_at within request time; owner list then omits it and direct owner lookup is 404. Restoring the three fixture entitlement fields and leaving through real membership routes restores all original declared rows, with only the new archived project retained.
